Bittensor Subnet 44 Validator Hotfix Update

We’ve released a new validator update to improve stability and fairness across the network. If you're running a validator, make sure to update as soon as possible.

✅ Max Processing Time Capped at 15s
- Slow hotkeys (e.g. 200s) were skewing speed score normalization
- Any response >15s now gets a speed score of 0
- Speed score normalization now uses the lesser of 15s or the observed max

✅ Unresponsive Hotkeys Penalized
- Previously, some hotkeys stayed active despite being unresponsive for up to 72h
- Now, a timeout = empty response = score penalty

Winning Metrics: How xG is calculated ⚽️

This stat is everywhere in modern football, from post-match debates to scouting reports - but what goes into the numbers?

Let’s break down the key factors behind this game-changing metric. ⬇️

Classic Kelly Criterion formula

b = net odds (decimal odds − 1)

p = your estimated win probability

f* = fraction of bankroll to stake

How to get sizing right? Enter: Kelly Criterion

Kelly Criterion helps you find the optimal % of your bankroll to stake on a +EV bet - where the true probability is higher than the bookie’s odds.

It maximizes long-term growth by calculating the ideal bet size based on your edge.

Fractional kelly for sustained growth with less volatility:

Whereas full kelly introduces risk for maximum growth, fractional kelly aims for growth in a risk-adjusted way, reducing the impact of a bad streak.

Fractional kelly could be implemented at any fraction of full kelly. E.g. 10%, 25%, 50%. The higher the percentage, the more risk you introduce.

DKING’s agentic wager

For this reason, DKING’s agentic wager will implement a 10% fractional kelly strategy, with a max allocation per single bet of 3%.

By doing so, it slashes variance yet keeps most of the compounding juice.

Kelly implementation exemplified:

Say there’s a bet with a 2.00 odd, but we’ve found a 25% +EV edge (we think there’s a higher probability than the bookies are assigning to an outcome)

The formula would look like this:
b = net odds = 2.00 − 1 = 1
p = true win probability = 0.625
1 − p = lose probability = 0.375
f* = (1 × 0.625 − 0.375) / 1
= 0.25

This means that your optimal bankroll allocation for this bet is calculated as 25%.

L;DR: Nail the stake, not just the pick.

 • Size every wager off an edge; Kelly shows the math
 • Shave it to 10-50 % Kelly for a lower risk, smoother ride
 • Compound edges, survive bad runs, let bankroll snowball 📈

Bankroll > hot takes. Bet smart, stay solvent. ♻️

Fractional kelly implementation

Using the same example, a fractional kelly of 10% would allocate 2.5% of total bankroll.

You can see how a fully kelly implementation invites a lot of risk. Lose 3 bets in a row where you allocate 25% of bankroll? You are down over half of your bankroll just from 3 bets.

Kelly only works if your edge is real.

In sports betting, your probability estimates are never perfect. Small errors can lead to oversizing and big losses.

Fractional Kelly helps manage that uncertainty. Bet smart. Compound consistently in a risk-adjusted manner.

Full kelly risk

While full Kelly aims to maximise growth, it still introduces notable risk, as:

• Volatility is enormous
 • A few mis-priced edges = ugly drawdowns
 • No buffer for model error

Bankroll ≠ Piggy Bank

Treat it like trading capital. Size badly and even a +EV edge goes broke.

Get sizing right and you can brick a week & still win the year.
